newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian farm lobby says Hanson threatens trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian farm lobby says Hanson threatens trade.

text.p: Australia's farm lobby on Thursday joined a chorus of criticism of far-right politician Pauline Hanson and said her views threatened rural trade with Asia.
National Farmers' Federation president Donald McGaughie told a seminar in Melbourne that food exports to the region were vulnerable to Hanson's stance against Asian immigration.
Australia's food exports to Asia are estimated to earn A$16 billion (US$12 billion) in foreign income by year 2000, he said.
"If the image of Australia as a commercial liability continues, those estimates will be simply wishful thinking," McGaughie told participants in a rural leadership programme.
He cited evidence that Australia's image had been damaged in some of its biggest export markets.
One Malaysian property investor has frozen a proposed A$40 million development due to concerns of racism here, he said.
Last month, a Melbourne-based cosmetics company said it was under pressure to remove "Australian made" labels from its Asian exports because of concerns of a consumer backlash in Asia.
The Australian government has also warned of the potential threat to trade from Hanson's views, which have struck a chord with voters around the country and won international publicity.
McGaughie on Thursday called for stronger and more consistent leadership to counter what he called Hanson's attempt to take Australia back to its protectionist, insulated past.
"No-one can turn back the clock and those of us with any kind of understanding of the world today wouldn't really want to," he said.
